intent.text: ses, on q1. Recommendation: remove Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) from the global ~/.claude/settings.json, or at minimum don't keep it global without a test. My reasons, from my vantage: the global file reloads live into every session on this machine, including ones that never agreed to this, so the blast radius of a wildcard allow is the whole machine, not this refactor. The README's safety argument rests on two things we have not verified: (1) that a wildcard after `export CC_AGENT=` cannot carry a chained command (e.g. `export CC_AGENT=x; rm -rf ...` or a newline-separated second command) past the rule. The README tests a `touch` after the export, but the rule is a prefix glob, and the claim that the harness splits it correctly is exactly what needs a test with `;`, `&&`, and newline variants. (2) how two PreToolUse hooks that both rewrite Bash combine; if a second hook's rewrite lands after the allow check, the rule matches a different string than intended. Until both are checked, a global allow is a bet on behalf of sessions that didn't place it. Options in order of my preference: (a) remove the global rule; accept the prompt friction for this refactor; (b) move the rule into the refactor project's own .claude/settings.json so only that tree is affected; (c) keep global only after the chained-command and double-hook tests pass and are recorded. I would not keep it global as-is. Joseph is the one who can judge the friction cost; I'd put the question to him as "is the prompt friction worth a machine-wide allow we haven't tested against chaining?"
